summary: Kickoff POC scoping focused on milestone map from kickoff through exec readout. Agreed success criteria (latency and throughput targets for two production workloads), access and security gating, initial benchmark plan, timeline with a 6-week execution window, and a mid-point review to validate metrics. Action items assigned for runbook, access, and benchmark artifacts.
topics: POC scope and primary use cases
Milestone timeline: kickoff, access setup, mid-point review, exec readout
transcript:
[00:00] Maya Patel: All right, thanks everyone for joining. We'll kick off in about a minute. Uh, Diego and I will run through the proposed milestone map and then dive into what we need from Orion to get access.
[00:12] Sofia Li: Sounds good, we have about an hour. Thanks, Maya.
[00:18] Diego Costa: Hi all, Diego here. Quick note: I'll be owning the benchmark plan and running the synthetic load. There may be a few name errors in the auto-transcript apologies in advance.
[00:30] Ethan Moore: No worries. First order of business — why don't we confirm the two workloads we said in the email: clinical note summarization (batch) and patient triage chat (low-latency chat) — is that still accurate?
[00:45] Maya Patel: Yes that's right — the POC will target two representative workloads: 1) nightly batch summarization of clinical notes — goal is throughput and cost per note; 2) interactive triage chat — goal is p95 latency under 350 ms and consistent responses.
[01:05] Sofia Li: For the chat, our current thresholds are p95 < 300-350ms and accuracy at least 87% on the labeled set. For summarization, we care about per-record cost and also ROUGE-like overlap with our reference.
[01:25] Markus Jensen: Quick infra note — we want to run in our VPC (private workload). Can Redwood run private connectors? We prefer not to send PHI outside our controlled network during testing.
[01:38] Maya Patel: Absolutely, Private is supported. For the POC we can do a scoped private deployment with a customer-managed VPC peering or a bastion agent depending on your org policies. We'll capture specifics in the access runbook.
[01:52] Priya Rao: On security: SOC 2 controls, KMS integration for keys, and audit logs are the essentials. Also we need to confirm data retention: logs should be purged after 30 days unless flagged.
[02:05] Aria Singh: Noted — we'll include a security checklist. Priya, will you send the more detailed control set or do you want us to propose one?
[02:12] Priya Rao: We'll send our baseline, but Redwood's template would help speed the review.
[02:20] Diego Costa: Moving to benchmarks — our plan is: step 1 generate synthetic payloads that mirror your size distributions; step 2 run three load profiles: nominal (10 QPS), bursty (50 QPS for 2 min), and stress (sustained 100 QPS) for the batch use case we focus on throughput in offline runs. For chat we'll do low concurrency p95 latency testing with warm KV cache and cold start checks.
[02:44] Markus Jensen: That sounds good. For the batch, our nightly window has about 8k notes, average 1.2k tokens per note, peaks to 12k occasionally. For chat, average session is 6 turns, median payload 450 tokens.
[02:59] Diego Costa: Perfect — that's the detail we need to size GPU capacity and suggest batching config.
[03:08] Ethan Moore: On success criteria — can we make it binary for the exec readout? e.g., two pass/fail gates: latency/throughput targets met AND quality metrics above thresholds.
[03:21] Maya Patel: Yes — recommend three gates: Access & security gate (all required network and key access), Operational gate (benchmarks for latency/throughput within agreed thresholds), and Quality gate (accuracy metrics and human eval samples). Exec readout will present pass/fail with remediation plan for any failures.
[03:40] Sofia Li: Does Redwood have a template for the quality evaluation? We want to avoid hand-waving at the exec level.
[03:48] Diego Costa: We do. I'll attach an evaluation template with sample prompts, scoring rubrics, and tooling for human-in-the-loop labels.
[03:56] Maya Patel: Timeline proposal: kickoff this week (today), access setup 1 week, baseline benchmarks week 2, mid-point review week 3, iteration and tuning weeks 4–5, exec readout week 6. So roughly a 6-week POC.
[04:14] Priya Rao: One week for access feels tight with our procurement for the bastion host. Can we plan parallel tasks so benching doesn't wait on full VPC peering?
[04:23] Aria Singh: Good point — we can do hybrid: Redwood hosted sandbox with anonymized samples to get baseline metrics while you finish VPC connectivity. Then swap to private for final runs.
[04:34] Markus Jensen: Hybrid flow works. We just need guarantees about no PHI in the hosted sandbox — we'll scrub samples.
[04:41] Maya Patel: We'll provide a scrubbed data template and a script to anonymize payloads — Diego will share.
[04:49] Diego Costa: I'll post the synthetic generator and example scripts in the shared drive.
[04:54] Ethan Moore: For reporting cadence — what do you recommend for artifacts at the mid-point review?
[05:01] Maya Patel: Mid-point should include: benchmark results (latency curves, throughput, token cost), sample quality evals (10–20 human-eval cases), incident log (any errors), and tuning actions taken. The exec readout will be condensed to one slide per gate plus recommended next steps.
[05:15] Sofia Li: Who owns the mid-point deck?
[05:19] Maya Patel: Redwood will prepare the initial mid-point deck; we'll invite Orion to co-edit.
[05:25] Priya Rao: About logging — we need to ensure PII redaction in transcripts and logs, and alerting for any anomalous exfil patterns. Is that configurable?
[05:36] Diego Costa: Yes, Redwood's logging pipeline can be configured to redact fields and forward only aggregated metrics. We'll include the logging config as part of the access runbook.
[05:46] Akward silence then chat beep– small cross talk
[05:54] Sofia Li: Slightly off topic — competitors. We've evaluated MegaCloud AI but their latencies on similar models were high. Curious if Redwood can produce a benchmark comparison later?
[06:05] Maya Patel: We can include comparative notches using open-model baselines; we'll avoid vendor-branded screenshots per your procurement guidance but can show anonymized baseline curves.
[06:17] Ethan Moore: Ok, timeline confirmation: kickoff today, access runbook by Monday (2025-11-24), initial hosted baselines in week of 2025-11-25, mid-point review around 2025-12-12, exec readout early Jan.
[06:32] Maya Patel: Correct. Any blockers?
[06:35] Markus Jensen: Need to confirm which data we can scrub and who will run the scrub script. We'll assign internally and reply.
[06:42] Priya Rao: Also need a short security questionnaire for our InfoSec review — is there a standard Redwood one?
[06:48] Aria Singh: Yes, we have an 18-question starter questionnaire and a SOC2 artifact bundle; I'll attach both.
[06:55] Sofia Li: One last question on rollbacks/fallbacks — if the private deployment shows an unexpected degradation, can Redwood route traffic to a hosted fallback during the POC?
[07:08] Diego Costa: Yes, we can configure routing policies for safe fallback, but that needs to be agreed up front and tested during the benchmark so triggers don't flip unexpectedly.
[07:19] Maya Patel: Great. Let's recap action items and owners — Diego, Maya, Markus, Priya — listed in the follow-up.
[07:29] Sofia Li: Thanks everyone. Looking forward to the run.
[07:33] Maya Patel: Thanks, meeting adjourned.
[07:36] [end of recording]
